A value of J ​ ( t ) ≈ 1.0 J(t)\approx 1.0 (implying λ m ​ a ​ x ≈ 0 \lambda_{max}\approx 0 ) indicates unitary (isometric) evolution, while exponential decay ( λ m ​ a ​ x < 0 \lambda_{max}<0 ) indicates dissipative dynamics characteristic of the vanishing gradient problem [ 51 ] . For the phase transition experiment (Fig. 1 ), all models were trained using curriculum learning to guarantee convergence to the ground state at T = 0 T=0 . The sequence length was incrementally increased from L = 1 L=1 to L = 5 L=5 only after the model achieved perfect accuracy on the current length. These pre-trained models were then subjected to thermal noise to generate the phase diagram. For the generalization experiment (Fig. 2 ), we employed a progressive curriculum where the maximum sequence length increased linearly from L = 10 L=10 to L = 50 L=50 over the first 70% of training steps.
